title: IMPLEMENTATION STATUS OF PM RAHAT SCHEME
body_text:
In accordance with the legal mandate under Section 162 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the PM-RAHAT (Road Accident Victims' Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment) scheme was launched for nationwide implementation on 13.02.2026, with the primary objective of reducing fatalities due to road accidents by ensuring timely and uninterrupted medical care to road accident victims including during the critical Golden Hour i.e., the time period lasting one hour following a traumatic injury during which there is highest likelihood of preventing death by providing prompt medical care. The scheme provides treatment cover upto Rs. 1.5 lakh per victim, subject to a maximum cap of 7 days from the date of accident on any category of road. Further, the treatment cover will be available to all those victims who are involved in road accidents caused by use of motor vehicles.
As on 31.07.2026 since the launch of the scheme for nation-wide implementation on 13.02.2026, a total of 22,481 victims have benefitted from the scheme across 34 States/UTs. The State/UT-wise details are attached as Annexure-I.
Against the total amount of the claims raised by the hospitals, State Health Agencies (SHA) have approved claims amounting to Rs.12.59 Crores. Out of which, Rs.10.56 Crores have been paid to the hospitals.
As per the Scheme guidelines notified vide S.O. 2489 (E) dated 04th June, 2025, designated hospitals under the Scheme, including empanelled hospitals under the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) that comply with the guidelines issued by the National Health Authority (NHA) for this scheme shall be deemed designated hospitals for the purposes of the Scheme.
Further, States & UTs are advised to designate and onboard additional hospitals based on detailed guidelines dated 20.5.2025 issued by NHA.
Denial of admission or treatment under the Scheme amounts to non-compliance with the applicable Scheme provisions. States/UTs are empowered to take action under laws regulating clinical establishments, including the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010, or the corresponding State-specific laws. Further, the hospital empanelment guidelines provide for disciplinary proceedings, suspension and de-empanelment in cases of non-compliance.
To ensure that victim reaches the hospital within Golden Hour, convergence with the 112 Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) has been established, so that a victim or Good Samaritan may dial 112 and obtain details of the nearest designated hospital and also seek ambulance support.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways informed Rajya Sabha about the implementation status of the PM-RAHAT scheme, launched nationwide on 13.02.2026 under Section 162 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, to provide cashless treatment up to Rs.1.5 lakh per road accident victim for 7 days. As of 31.07.2026, 22,481 victims across 34 States/UTs had benefitted, with SHAs approving claims worth Rs.12.59 crore and Rs.10.56 crore already disbursed to hospitals. Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh recorded the highest number of cases.
enrichment.context: PM-RAHAT builds on the cashless treatment scheme for road accident victims notified earlier and formalizes the 'Golden Hour' concept—the critical first hour after trauma when prompt medical intervention significantly improves survival chances. India has one of the highest road accident fatality rates globally, and delays in initiating treatment due to hospitals demanding police clearance or payment upfront have historically worsened outcomes; this scheme addresses that by mandating treatment first and reimbursement later through designated/empanelled hospitals, leveraging the existing Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY hospital network. The scheme's convergence with the 112 Emergency Response Support System aims to reduce response time by directing victims/Good Samaritans to the nearest designated hospital and dispatching ambulances swiftly. This complements earlier legal reforms like the Good Samaritan Law protections and mandatory e-DAR (electronic Detailed Accident Report) integration, which enables police verification of accident cases within a time-bound framework, and reflects the government's broader push to reduce road accident fatalities as targeted under the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 and India's commitments under the Brasilia Declaration on road safety.

prelims_questions.question: The PM-RAHAT scheme, aimed at providing cashless treatment to road accident victims, has been implemented under which legal provision?
options: Section 134 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
Section 162 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
Section 198 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
Section 279 of the Indian Penal Code
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states the scheme was launched in accordance with the legal mandate under Section 162 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

prelims_questions.question: Under the PM-RAHAT scheme, what is the maximum treatment cover and time period within which the victim must be treated after a road accident?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release specifies treatment cover of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh per victim, subject to a maximum cap of 7 days from the date of accident.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the 'Golden Hour' concept in road accident trauma care in India. Evaluate the effectiveness of schemes like PM-RAHAT in reducing road accident fatalities, and suggest measures to improve last-mile implementation.

mains_questions.question: India continues to record one of the highest numbers of road accident deaths globally despite various legislative and policy interventions.
